title: IoT & Cloud
blurb: Publishing sensor data to the cloud.

topics.name: MQTT Protocol
topics.question: What is MQTT and how does publish/subscribe work
topics.assetAlt: MQTT publish–subscribe topology: sensor clients publish values such as “30°” on topic “temp” to a central MQTT broker, which forwards each message to the valve and cloud-server clients subscribed to that topic.

sections.heading: Publish / subscribe
paragraphs: Devices do not talk directly. A publisher sends a message to a named topic on a central broker; any client subscribed to that topic receives it. This decouples your Arduino from the dashboard and scales to many devices.

sections.heading: Topics and QoS
paragraphs: Topics are hierarchical strings (`esi/3cc3/temp`). Quality-of-Service levels trade delivery guarantees for overhead, and an auth token usually gates who may publish to a topic.

topics.hint: Data that never reaches the cloud is usually a topic, token, or broker-address typo — check the exact (case-sensitive) topic string first, then the credentials, then the broker host/port.

topics.name: ThingsBoard Cloud
topics.question: How do I exchange LabVIEW data with ThingsBoard Cloud
topics.assetAlt: MQTT publish–subscribe topology: sensor clients publish values such as “30°” on topic “temp” to a central MQTT broker, which forwards each message to the valve and cloud-server clients subscribed to that topic.
topics.summary: Publish JSON telemetry, receive persistent shared attributes, and build a device dashboard.

sections.heading: One cloud device per physical project
paragraphs: ThingsBoard stores measurements as telemetry and persistent cloud-to-device settings as shared attributes. Build gauges, time-series charts, indicators, and controls around the same device entity.

sections.heading: MQTT connection and topics
paragraphs: Connect to `mqtt.thingsboard.cloud` on port 1883 with the device access token as the username and a blank password. Publish JSON to `v1/devices/me/telemetry` and exchange desired-state values through the ThingsBoard attribute topics.

topics.hint: An empty widget means a token, label, or rate-limit problem — verify the token is the device token (not the account token), the variable label matches exactly, and you are under the free-tier limit.

topics.name: ThingsBoard shared attributes
topics.question: How do shared attributes preserve cloud-to-device desired state
topics.assetAlt: MQTT publish–subscribe topology: sensor clients publish values such as “30°” on topic “temp” to a central MQTT broker, which forwards each message to the valve and cloud-server clients subscribed to that topic.
topics.summary: Store desired state in the cloud and request the current value after startup or reconnect.

sections.heading: Core idea
paragraphs: Use `led_switch` and `moisture_threshold` as persistent shared attributes. Subscribe for changes and issue a startup request so LabVIEW recovers the current desired value after reconnecting.

sections.heading: Where it is used
paragraphs: Used in Lab 7 and Lab 8. Prerequisites: ThingsBoard Cloud, MQTT, and a device dashboard.

topics.hint: On startup, subscribe before publishing the shared-attribute request; parse both live updates and response envelopes before applying validated values.

sections.heading: Core idea
paragraphs: The site is static first: index, labs, knowledge, and assets can be hosted together. A later LMS connection should use an approved institutional method such as LTI.
